theorem moduleCup_canonical_hzero_identification (F G : C) :
    let F₀ := (CochainComplex.singleFunctor C 0).obj F
    let G₀ := (CochainComplex.singleFunctor C 0).obj G
    let c := Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ Q F₀ G₀ ≫ Q.map (moduleCup_singleTensorIso F G).hom
    IsIso ((homologyFunctor C 0).map c) ∧
      ∀ (P : CochainComplex C ℤ) (p : P ⟶ F₀)
        [P.IsStrictlyLE 0] [QuasiIso p]
        (_hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, ObjectProperty.flat (P.X i))
        (hP : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso C (.up ℤ)).kFlat P),
        c =
          (tensorIso (asIso (Q.map p)) (Iso.refl (Q.obj G₀))).inv ≫
            (QObjTensorQObjIsoOfKFlatLeft P G₀ hP).hom ≫
            Q.map (p ⊗ₘ 𝟙 G₀) ≫ Q.map (moduleCup_singleTensorIso F G).hom

title: Canonical derived-to-ordinary H-zero identification with flat-model transport
statement: Let C be a braided closed monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with monoidal additivity, functorial flat resolutions and a derived category. For objects F,G let F₀,G₀ denote their single complexes in degree zero and e their canonical total-tensor/single-tensor isomorphism, constructed from map₂HomologicalComplexFlipObjSingleIso followed by singleMapHomologicalComplex. Set c=μ_Q(F₀,G₀) followed by Q(e.hom). H-zero(c) is invertible. For every strictly nonpositive termwise-flat K-flat resolution p:P→F₀, c equals the inverse of tensorIso(asIso(Qp),refl(QG₀)), followed by QObjTensorQObjIsoOfKFlatLeft(P,G₀), Q(p tensor id), and Q(e.hom). Thus the canonical comparison is precisely the transported flat-model augmentation, not an unspecified isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose a nonpositive flat resolution; it is K-flat. The model H-zero identification follows from the cokernel calculation and right exactness of tensor. Naturality of the lax monoidal comparison of Q identifies its component with the explicitly recorded transport through the localized resolution and QObjTensorQObjIsoOfKFlatLeft. Tensoring Qp with the identity is an isomorphism; therefore transporting the model calculation gives invertibility of H-zero(c). The real single-tensor isomorphism e identifies the codomain with Q((F tensor G)[0]).
